inputs.message: I keep mixing up when Spanish se is reflexive or passive.

expected_ideas: se is not translated the same way every time
the sentence pattern helps decide what se is doing

misconception_markers.description: Learner evidence may match the pattern: se one fixed translation.
misconception_markers.label: se one fixed translation

misconception_markers.description: Learner evidence may match the pattern: se sentence subject confusion.
misconception_markers.label: se sentence subject confusion

presentation_support.text: Uses bus/train transfer maps as a structural support for the target language-pattern operation. The support is meant to reveal the hidden operation, not decorate the example.

prompt.full_prompt:
Think of se like a marker on a transit map: the same small symbol can point to different routes depending on where it appears.

Look at these:
1. Se lava. = He/she washes himself/herself.
2. Se habla español. = Spanish is spoken / People speak Spanish.
3. Se me cayó el vaso. = The glass fell on me.

Which idea will help most?
prompt.reshaping_explanation: Probe asks the smallest task that reveals the hidden distinction; interest is structurally tied to the repair target.
prompt.root_problem_explanation: Surface confusion: se appears in several sentences. Hidden mistake: the learner is forcing one English translation onto se instead of using the sentence pattern to decide what job se is doing. Repair target: shift from word-for-word translation to route-matching: each sentence pattern sends se to a different job.
